title: Microsoft Purview: retention policies to delete Microsoft Teams call logs
notes: claim 48: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the deletion explanation omits the holds that can suspend permanent deletion, so a configured period is not an unconditional compliance deadline. The impact rationale also says nothing changes without administrator action, despite the documented removal of new call records from existing Teams chat policies.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The policy reaches only call logs created after it is configured and active, not older gap records.
claims.quote: The policy applies only to new call logs that are created after the policy is configured and active.

claims.claim: The call-log policy includes logs from Teams chats and Teams channels.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Before late April 2026, chat and channel CDRs were included in Teams chat retention policies.
claims.quote: Prior to supporting the retention of Teams call logs in late April 2026, CDRs for Teams chat and Teams channels were included in retention policies for the Teams chat location.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: New CDRs are now supported only by a Teams call-log policy, not existing Teams chat policies.
claims.quote: Going forward, new CDRs are supported only when you create a retention policy for Teams call logs.

claims.claim: CDRs already included in earlier Teams chat retention policies remain managed by those policies.
claims.quote: CDRs included in previous Teams chat retention policies continue to be managed by those same policies.

claims.claim: New-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy with Name, Applications User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog and ExchangeLocation All creates the policy targeting all mailboxes.
claims.quote: "User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog"; The ExchangeLocation parameter specifies the mailboxes to include in the policy. Valid values are: ... The value All for all mailboxes. You can only use this value by itself.

claims.claim: New-AppRetentionComplianceRule with Name, Policy, RetentionDuration in days and RetentionComplianceAction Delete sets the deletion rule.
claims.quote: The RetentionDuration parameter specifies the hold duration for the retention rule. Valid values are: An integer: The hold duration in days. ... The RetentionComplianceAction parameter specifies the retention action for the rule. Valid values are: Delete

claims.claim: New-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy with Name, Applications User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog and RestrictiveRetention $true enables Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: The RestrictiveRetention parameter specifies whether Preservation Lock is enabled for the policy. Valid values are: $true: Preservation Lock is enabled for the policy.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal control to create or configure the call-log policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention policy portal create modify Preservation Lock RestrictiveRetention delete only. Opened create-retention-policies: creation and modification are PowerShell-only; the portal is read-only.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal control to set the call-log deletion period.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention policy portal create modify Preservation Lock RestrictiveRetention delete only. Opened create-retention-policies and new-appretentioncompliancerule; the portal is read-only and PowerShell sets the duration.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal control to apply Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention policy portal create modify Preservation Lock RestrictiveRetention delete only; Preservation Lock delete-only. Opened retention-preservation-lock: enabling this feature is not available in the UI.

claims.claim: The printed Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users path adds users to a Purview role group.
claims.quote: On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role-group> -Member <user-UPN> grants membership and the group's effective permissions.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Preservation Lock is irreversible and prevents disabling or turning off the policy.
claims.quote: No one -- including an administrator -- can turn off the policy or make it less restrictive. ... After a policy is locked, no one can turn off or disable it, or remove apps from the policy.

claims.claim: A locked policy can be increased or extended but not reduced.
claims.quote: A locked policy can be increased or extended, but it can't be reduced, disabled, or turned off.

claims.claim: Nothing deletes call logs until an administrator creates the call-log policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention deletion eDiscovery hold Litigation Hold permanent deletion; Teams call logs retention licensing Business Basic F3 pay as you go billing meter. Read retention-policies-teams and PSTN usage report excerpts; no universal absence of other deletion routes is stated.
claims.fix: Remove 'Nothing deletes them until an administrator creates the call log policy.' The preceding sentence already states the documented default without claiming that no other deletion route exists.

claims.claim: The configured deletion process runs automatically rather than requiring an approval for each record.
claims.quote: The record is retained there for at least 1 day and then permanently deleted the next time the timer job runs (typically between 1-7 days).

claims.claim: Expired call-related records move to SubstrateHolds typically 1-7 days after expiry.
claims.quote: At the end of the retention period, the call-related record is moved to the SubstrateHolds folder. This action typically takes between 1-7 days from the expiry date.

claims.claim: Call-related records remain in SubstrateHolds for at least one day.
claims.quote: The record is retained there for at least 1 day

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The policy permanently deletes expired call-log records at the next timer run, typically 1-7 days later, without qualification.
claims.quote: For all examples that refer to permanent deletion, because of the principles of retention, this action is suspended if the message is subject to another retention policy to retain the item or it's subject to an eDiscovery hold.
claims.fix: Add to the deletion explanation and qualify the After rollout deletion advice: 'Permanent deletion is suspended while the record is subject to an applicable retention policy that retains it or an eDiscovery hold.' The call-log section explicitly applies Example 3's behaviour and timings; see https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-teams.
